content.rationale: every pointer and keyboard behaviour plus the visual states they drive, with the selected node rendered bolder than the related and hover-neighbour elements; each state change is applied incrementally (stppxysx): interact.ts learns the drawn elements once per graph revision - a node per data-node-id and the visible parts of each data-edge-key, queried at attach and rebuilt only when the graph is swapped - so a later change looks its elements up by the identity it carries instead of scanning the surface; a selection or hover derives the emphasised node and edge sets from the model's incidence index and writes a class only to the elements entering or leaving those sets; and a drag records each pointer position in a pending map and applies it in one relayout per animation frame, the last position of a node winning so nothing is dropped; a lookup that misses ends that change rather than falling back to a scan. Selection emphasis holds its viewport-change bound through to the displayed surface (mntwwzyl): interact.css expresses both highlighting of selected, related and hover-neighbour elements (.is-selected with accent border and 3px outline, [data-node-id].is-related / .is-hover-neighbour with accent border and 2px outline, and .edge.is-related / .is-hover-neighbour with accent stroke) and dimming of unrelated elements (.is-dimmed, .is-dimmed .node__label-secondary, and .edge.is-dimmed variants with resolved text, border and stroke colours mixed in sRGB at 0.3 against --surface) exclusively through passive resolved appearance properties that settle when selection changes, without any per-dimmed-element or per-brightened-element opacity or filter stacking surface, compositing group or blend pass; and every viewport change (pan, zoom, pinch, wheel, fit and resize) writes only the single surface transform via applyViewport without walking, querying, re-classing, restyling or refreshing the dimmed or brightened elements, without throttling or dropping viewport updates, and without suppressing emphasis during pan or zoom. A pointer gesture also keeps the subject it was pressed on: at the press interact.ts resolves the node under the pointer once, or records that the press landed on an edge or on empty canvas, and the gesture's later events act on that recorded subject instead of reading their event target, which the browser addresses to the canvas once the press has set pointer capture. A double click therefore asks the editor for the document of the node its gesture was pressed on, a second double click on another node asks for that node and not the first, and a double click on empty canvas asks for no node's document; a press that becomes a drag, a pan or a pinch fixes no double-click subject, and a double click delivered with no gesture behind it still resolves from the element it is addressed to.
